title: He Dreamed His Ship Would Sink — Then 211 People Vanished Without a Trace
description:
In July 1909, passenger Claude Sawyer had three nightmares in a row: a sword-wielding figure rising from a blood-red sea, and his ship, the SS Waratah, rolling over and sinking. Terrified, he begged to leave the voyage and got off at Durban. Two days later, the Waratah vanished with 211 people aboard, last seen near the Bashee River mouth with no distress signal ever sent.

No wreckage. No lifeboats. No bodies. Search ships scoured over 14,000 square miles of ocean for months and found nothing. Investigators later discovered the ship had already shown dangerous instability on her maiden voyage, tilting so severely passengers nearly went overboard — and the owners sent her out again anyway.

For more than a century, wreck hunters have chased sonar hits and rusted hull fragments off South Africa's Wild Coast, but none have ever been confirmed as the Waratah. Somewhere down there, or nowhere at all, the ship and everyone aboard remain one of maritime history's greatest unsolved mysteries.
